requirements.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed service on node1.
requirements.summary: OpenRC shows inventory-api enabled and started. The endpoint returns healthy JSON, the listener runs as uid 65534 with oom_score_adj=-900, and the same configuration and behavior recovered after reboot.

requirements.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving when system-wide memory pressure causes an out-of-memory event.
requirements.summary: The endpoint was healthy immediately before the bounded stress test and remained responsive with the service started after the OOM kill. The protected listener retained PID 3028 across the event, supporting that it survived rather than being restarted.

requirements.requirement: The memory hog, rather than inventory-api, is stopped by the kernel.
requirements.summary: The hog was launched with oom_score_adj=1000. Kernel logs directly identify stress-ng-vm PID 3443 as the process killed by the global OOM event, while inventory-api remained healthy.

overall_summary: The task outcomes are satisfied. inventory-api is managed, enabled, responsive, and strongly disfavored for OOM selection; a bounded global OOM event directly killed the high-score memory hog while the API listener survived and remained healthy. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed coherently. Hygiene is reduced only by retained test artifacts and test packages.
limitations: No HTTP request was captured while the hog was still demonstrably alive because it had already exited before the follow-up poll. Survival is nevertheless strongly supported by the unchanged inventory-api listener PID before and after the kernel-recorded OOM event.
The lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported on Alpine; direct OpenRC status observations instead establish inventory-api health.
A final package inventory was not captured, so retention of stress-ng and its dependencies is based on the completed installation and absence of any removal command in the complete timeline.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing actions had a clear task or verification role; no unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. The initial failed service start created configuration reused by the corrected solution and was therefore not unnecessary. Two hygiene defects remained: the OOM test left /tmp/inventory-oom-test.log and /tmp/inventory-oom-test.pid, directly confirmed by the final snapshot, and stress-ng plus four dependencies were installed for testing with no removal captured. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service and payload state were all observed and independently corroborated.
